![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/c2a8da9dd6d088d30b0b023d50ebf2c23e2bcfda89cd390ec16779694ae5eb39.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $y={x}^{3}$ and $y=x$ in the first quadrant is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=2.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3} & =x \\ {x}^{3}-x & =0 \\ x({x}^{2}-1) & =0 \\ x & =-1,0,1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

Now, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/82783afd970ec3f0e90a8b97a12207b0ed8cbf82323e0512e9fe36b99a6fdc2f.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=x,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y={x}^{3}.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y={x}^{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/4a9a72a194226f73da234e03b93e4b255849315808ac948c0958d8dee52b4f73.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(2)-({x}^{3})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[2-{x}^{3}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/4c53b4b1ad169119cadf490636b12235b3fc225a08d57c11d4f8e26318797f25.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(2)-(x)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[2-x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[2-{x}^{3}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[2-x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[2-{x}^{3}]}^{2}-{[2-x]}^{2})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
